chains.title: C250T creates a de novo ETS site bound by GABPA/GABPB1, driving monoallelic TERT reactivation in glioblastoma
chains.element: TERT core promoter, -250 bp from ATG (chr5:1295135)
chains.cell_type: Glioma stem/progenitor cells and glioblastoma tumour cells

links.claim: The alt (A on plus strand; C>T on the TERT-coding minus strand) allele generates a canonical 5'-GGAA-3' ETS core that is absent from the ref allele; among ETS factors the GABPA/GABPB1 heterotetramer is selected because it uniquely requires two ETS sites in the correct spacing, which the new site plus the native ETS site at -200 provides, and because GABPA is ubiquitously expressed in glioma lines.
The new site lies in the TERT core promoter, which carries active-promoter chromatin marks and acquires H3K4me2/3 selectively on the mutant allele.
GABPA/GABPB1 recruitment activates transcription of TERT specifically from the mutant allele, giving modest but sufficient telomerase reactivation.
Glioblastoma cells (and melanoma, bladder urothelium) lack an alternative telomere-maintenance route and depend on this reactivation; GABPA is expressed in these cells.
Restored telomerase permits unlimited replicative capacity, enabling tumour outgrowth and conferring the poor prognosis associated with TERT promoter mutations in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.

predictions: GABPA and GABPB1 ChIP shows allele-specific occupancy at the mutant TERT promoter and no occupancy at wild-type promoters.
GABPA or GABPB1L knockdown selectively reduces TERT mRNA in C250T/C228T-mutant lines but not in TERT-promoter-wildtype lines.
Reporter assays with the mutant promoter lose activity when the created GGAA is scrambled or when the spacing to the native -200 ETS site is altered.
falsified_if: GABPA/GABPB1 ChIP shows no enrichment at the mutant allele.
GABPA knockdown leaves TERT expression unchanged in mutant lines while another ETS factor's knockdown does reduce it.

chains.title: The de novo ETS site is bound by ETS1 rather than GABPA

links.claim: The alt allele creates a GGAA core matching the ETS consensus; ETS1 is chosen within the ETS group because it is expressed in glioma and melanoma and has been reported to activate mutant TERT promoters downstream of MAPK signalling.
The site sits in the TERT core promoter and becomes nucleosome-depleted on the mutant allele.
ETS1 binding increases TERT transcription from the mutant allele.
ETS1 levels are MAPK-dependent, so the effect is strongest in cells with active RAS/BRAF-MEK-ERK signalling, common in glioblastoma and melanoma.
Telomerase reactivation sustains proliferation and tumour growth.

predictions: MEK inhibition lowers TERT mRNA in mutant lines proportionally to ETS1 activity, independently of GABPA levels.
ETS1 ChIP, not GABPA ChIP, shows allele-specific occupancy.
ETS1 knockdown reduces mutant-allele TERT expression.
falsified_if: ETS1 knockdown does not change TERT levels in mutant lines.
No ETS1 ChIP signal at the TERT promoter in mutant cells.

chains.title: The created site is bound by ELK4 (TCF subfamily) acting with serum-response signalling

links.claim: The alt allele creates a GGAA core compatible with TCF-subfamily ETS binding; ELK4 is chosen within this group because it is broadly expressed in glioma lines and binds single ETS sites without a partner.
Binding occurs in the TERT core promoter immediately upstream of the transcription start site.
ELK4 recruitment raises TERT transcription from the mutant allele.
Effect requires ERK-phosphorylated ELK4, so it tracks with growth-factor signalling in glioblastoma cells.
Telomere maintenance supports continued tumour cell division.

predictions: ELK4 knockdown reduces TERT in mutant but not wild-type lines.
Allele-specific ELK4 ChIP signal at the TERT promoter.
Single-site reporter (new GGAA only, native -200 site deleted) retains activity, unlike the GABPA model.
falsified_if: ELK4 depletion has no effect on TERT.
Activity of the mutant reporter strictly requires the second, native ETS site.

chains.title: The created site is bound by ELF1, which is the functional activator at the mutant promoter

links.claim: ELF-subfamily factors prefer AGGAAGT-like sequences; the alt allele produces such a core, and ELF1 is chosen within the group for its high and near-universal expression in tumour lines.
The site is within the TERT core promoter and gains accessibility on the mutant allele.
ELF1 occupancy increases TERT transcription from the mutant allele.
ELF1 is abundant in glioblastoma lines, so the effect does not depend on a signalling-regulated partner.
Sustained telomerase activity supports immortalisation and tumour progression.

predictions: ELF1 ChIP shows allele-specific occupancy; GABPA does not.
ELF1 knockdown reduces TERT in mutant lines.
TERT levels correlate with ELF1 expression across mutant glioblastoma lines.
falsified_if: No ELF1 enrichment at the mutant promoter.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of this specific base change
predictions: Editing only this base into a TERT-promoter-wildtype glioblastoma line changes neither TERT mRNA nor telomerase activity.
Mutant and wildtype alleles show equal nascent TERT transcription in heterozygous lines.
No TF shows differential occupancy between alleles.
falsified_if: Single-base knock-in raises TERT expression or telomerase activity.
Allele-specific TERT expression is seen in heterozygous mutant tumours.

matrix.test: GABPA and GABPB1 ChIP-qPCR (or CUT&RUN) at the TERT promoter in a C250T-mutant versus promoter-wildtype glioblastoma line

outcomes.outcome: Strong mutant-specific GABPA and GABPB1 signal
No or weak GABPA signal; ETS1 signal instead
No allele-specific signal for any factor

matrix.test: siRNA/shRNA knockdown panel (GABPA, GABPB1, ETS1, ELK4, ELF1) with TERT RT-qPCR in mutant and wildtype lines

outcomes.outcome: GABPA/GABPB1 knockdown lowers TERT only in mutant lines
No knockdown changes mutant-specific TERT levels

matrix.test: Luciferase reporter with mutant promoter, with and without the native -200 ETS site, plus scrambled new GGAA

outcomes.outcome: Activity needs both ETS sites (multimeric GABP requirement)
Mutant and reference reporters are equally active

matrix.test: CRISPR single-base knock-in of C250T into a TERT-promoter-wildtype line; measure allele-specific TERT and telomerase activity
MEK inhibitor treatment of mutant lines with TERT RT-qPCR

next_experiment: Run a single ChIP-qPCR/CUT&RUN panel for GABPA, GABPB1 and ETS1 at the TERT core promoter in one C250T-mutant and one promoter-wildtype glioblastoma line: mutant-specific GABPA+GABPB1 enrichment supports H1, while ETS1-only enrichment supports H2, and absence of any allele-specific occupancy supports the null.
